title: SAML 2.0 setup wizard: metadata sentinel and operator rollback playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a robust SAML 2.0 Setup Wizard experience that validates incoming IdP metadata with a scoring 'sentinel' so operators can safely accept, quarantine, or roll back metadata changes. This ticket implements: 1) a metadata sentinel that performs schema validation, XML signature verification, certificate chain and fingerprint checks, and heuristics (clock skew, unexpected endpoints, binding changes); 2) a dry-run validation mode that simulates live traffic using a replay harness and produces acceptance metrics; 3) an operator rollback playbook and UI affordances (preview diff, approve/reject, staged apply with canary assertions); and 4) audit-log events and RBAC v2 enforcement hooks to record who approved what and to limit who can accept high-risk changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Wizard rejects metadata with invalid XML signatures and marks as 'broken' in the preview.
2) Dry-run produces a validation report with a numeric risk score and example assertion replays.
3) Admins with 'saml_admin' role can approve high-risk delta; users without role cannot.
4) Every metadata change creates immutable audit events (metadata.upload, metadata.preview, metadata.approve, metadata.apply, metadata.rollback) containing diff and operator id.
5) Rollback can be executed via Console and the API, reverting metadata and emitting a metadata.rollback audit event.
6) End-to-end tests pass in the staging cluster (replay harness + canary assertions).
implementation_notes:
Technical approach: build a standalone 'metadata-sentinel' service inside auth-infra; it accepts uploaded/URL-provided metadata and returns a validation bundle (flat JSON stringified in response). Sentinel runs: 1) XML canonicalization and signature verification; 2) X509 chain validation using customer/public CA store + trust anchors; 3) fingerprint delta and thumbprint heuristics (detect cert rotation vs suspicious replacement); 4) schema-aware diff against current metadata (list changed entityIDs, endpoints, bindings, attributes); 5) traffic dry-run: spawn synthetic AuthNRequests via a replay harness to existing assertion simulator (see test_plan). Record per-check findings as tagged strings rather than nested objects to keep logs searchable.
Trade-offs: doing a full assertion replay on every metadata change is expensive; we will gate full replay to high-risk (>0.6) scores. Low-risk changes run a fast path that validates signatures and certs only.
APIs/PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-infra/pull/1289, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6542.
Design spec: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aSAMLWizardSpec
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for XML signature edge cases (enveloped, detached).
2) Integration tests: upload metadata with cert chain issues, expired cert, and unexpected endpoint; verify sentinel flags correctly.
3) Dry-run harness tests: simulate AuthNRequest roundtrip and validate canary assertions succeed against test IdP.
4) RBAC gating tests: ensure only 'saml_admin' role can approve high-risk changes (use infra-test tenant).
5) Audit verification: ingest generated audit events into logging pipeline and assert presence of expected fields.
6) Chaos test: partially apply metadata to canary hosts and confirm automatic rollback trigger if >10% of canary assertions fail.
rollout_plan:
Phased rollout:
- Phase 1 (staging): enable sentinel in dry-run-only mode for all uploads (monitor health).
- Phase 2 (beta orgs): enable preview + manual approve flow for orgs opted into 'strict-sso'.
- Phase 3 (wide): enable gating for high-risk deltas by default; send post-apply validation checks and 24h audit retention for change artifacts.
Feature flags: 'saml.sentinel.dry_run' and 'saml.sentinel.gate_high_risk'.
Rollback: operator may trigger console 'Revert metadata' which calls sentinel.rollback endpoint and replays last-good metadata, emits metadata.rollback audit event.
open_questions:
1) What threshold numeric score should be classified as 'high-risk'? Suggest default 0.6 but product may want 0.5.
2) Do we allow automatic soft-accept of cert rotations if only fingerprint changes but endpoints identical? Security prefers manual approval.
3) Storage policy for archived metadata diffs — legal wants 7 years, infra prefers 90 days.
4) Who owns the UI copy for the risk explanations? Assign to design.
5) Do we surface raw IdP metadata XML in audit logs or redact sensitive elements? Default: redact AssertionConsumerService URLs in logs unless admin role.
